extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and invited peer reviewers for PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting peer review of manuscripts submitted to PLOS ONE, describing the publication criteria reviewers must check, the review form structure, and reviewer responsibilities (timeliness, conflicts, confidentiality, co-review credit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Research
rubrics_metrics.description: "The study presents the results of original research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must report original research (not reviews, opinions, or republished results). This is one of seven mandatory publication criteria that must be satisfied for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: "Results reported have not been published elsewhere"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data and findings must be unpublished elsewhere; duplicate or redundant publication is not acceptable. Report any overlap or prior publication in your review comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: "Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether experimental design, data collection, statistical analyses, and other analytic methods are appropriate and executed to a high standard. Check that methods are described with enough detail to allow replication and that analyses are correctly applied and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the claims and interpretations follow logically from the presented data and analyses. Flag overstated conclusions or inferences not supported by the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the manuscript is readable and understandable. Note major language issues that impede comprehension; minor copyediting can be handled separately, but unintelligible prose is a problem for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: "The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify ethical approvals, consent, and adherence to relevant ethical standards (e.g., human/animal subject protections, research integrity). Report any ethical concerns in your confidential and/or public comments as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & Reporting Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the manuscript follows relevant reporting checklists (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA where applicable) and PLOS ONE data availability expectations. Ensure data sharing statements and access to underlying data are present and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focus: Technical rigor and ethics (not importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE evaluates whether papers demonstrate "technical rigor" and meet scientific and ethical standards for the published record rather than assessing "importance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending a decision, reviewers should focus on methodological soundness, validity of data and analyses, ethical compliance, and clarity — not on perceived novelty or impact. Comments should address whether the work meets the publication criteria rather than ranking its importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Structure — Comments to Authors (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments to Authors: Questions 1-4: Yes/No/I don't know/N/A responses with details; Question 5: Main review text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured answers to the form's initial checklist questions with brief supporting details, then supply the main review as free-text (Question 5) that explains strengths, weaknesses, and required revisions. These comments are shared with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Structure — Comments to Editor (confidential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments to Editor (confidential): competing interests declaration; collaborator names; publication highlight recommendations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the confidential section to disclose competing interests, list collaborators or other relevant relationships, and suggest whether the manuscript is suitable for any highlight/press features. Do not include text here that authors need to see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to submit evaluations promptly (within the stated 10-day window). If unable to meet the deadline, inform the editorial office so alternative arrangements can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing Interests Declaration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must disclose any financial or non-financial conflicts that could bias their review. Declare these in the Comments to Editor section and follow journal policy on what constitutes a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat manuscript content and review correspondence as confidential. Do not share or discuss the manuscript with others unless explicitly permitted by the editor (e.g., for co-reviewing with acknowledgment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit Co-reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you involve trainees or colleagues in the review process, disclose and credit them according to journal procedures (so their contributions are recognized). Follow PLOS ONE's co-review policy when naming collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider key evaluation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider methodology, data support, literature context, protocol adherence, reproducibility, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In your review assess: appropriateness and rigor of methodology; whether data support the conclusions; situating results within existing literature; adherence to pre-registered protocols or methods; potential for reproducibility; and clarity of presentation. Provide concrete examples and suggested revisions where problems are identified.
